database_summary: Small brewery/retail operational schema with products, purchases, inventory, orders and web analytics. Mix of descriptive dimension tables (products, product_groups, packaging, channels_dim, gender_dim, customers, breweries, stock), event/history tables (purchases, monthly_sales, monthly_budget, ticker, web_counter_hist, web_page_visits, server_heartbeat, picking_log, emp_hire_periods) and current-state tables (inventory, orders, orderlines, picking_list, picking_line). Several helper/collection-style text columns (customer_favorites.favorite_list, customer_reviews.review_list) encode lists in strings. Many tables are normalized but some composite PKs are represented across multiple columns. Foreign keys exist but multiplicity should be considered for joins (e.g. products -> monthly_sales/purchases/inventory/orderlines produce multiplicative rows).

accepted.name: product_monthly_sales
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  mth,
  SUM(qty) AS qty
FROM monthly_sales
GROUP BY product_id, mth
accepted.description: Aggregated monthly sales per product. Useful for time-series comparisons, joins to product metadata, budgeting, and trend calculations. | Use for: Compare month-over-month product sales; Join product sales to products or product_groups; Compute growth rates or rolling averages per product

accepted.name: product_inventory_current
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  location_id,
  SUM(qty) AS qty
FROM inventory
GROUP BY product_id, location_id
accepted.description: Current inventory quantities summed by product and location. Useful for stock-level reports, reordering decisions, and joining to product minimums. | Use for: Check stock per product and location; Identify products below minimums after joining product_minimums; Allocate inventory to orders or picklists

accepted.name: products_with_group
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.id AS id,
  p.name AS name,
  p.group_id AS group_id,
  pg.name AS name_group
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN product_groups pg ON p.group_id = pg.id
accepted.description: Products enriched with their product group name. Use when reporting product attributes alongside group/category. | Use for: List products with category names; Filter products by group name and join to sales or inventory; Aggregate sales by product group

accepted.name: orders_with_line_totals
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ol.id AS id,
  ol.order_id AS order_id,
  o.customer_id AS customer_id,
  o.ordered AS ordered,
  o.delivery AS delivery,
  ol.product_id AS product_id,
  ol.qty AS qty,
  ol.amount AS amount
FROM orderlines ol
LEFT JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.id
accepted.description: Order lines joined to orders and customers, exposing order-level attributes with line measures. Useful for order-level and customer-level analyses and revenue calculations. | Use for: Compute revenue or quantities per order or per customer; Join orders to products, customers, or shipping dates; Analyze order fulfillment and delivery lag

accepted.name: web_devices_daily_totals
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT day, 'pc' AS device_type, pc AS cnt FROM web_devices
UNION ALL
SELECT day, 'tablet' AS device_type, tablet AS cnt FROM web_devices
UNION ALL
SELECT day, 'phone' AS device_type, phone AS cnt FROM web_devices
accepted.description: Unpivot web device counts into one row per day per device_type with count. Useful for trend charts and joining with other daily web metrics. | Use for: Plot device-type trends over time; Join daily device counts to web_demographics or web_counter_hist by day

accepted.name: web_demographics_unpivot

SELECT day, 'M' AS gender, 'tw' AS channel, 'cnt' AS metric, m_tw_cnt AS value FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day, 'M' AS gender, 'tw' AS channel, 'qty' AS metric, m_tw_qty AS value FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day, 'M' AS gender, 'fb' AS channel, 'cnt' AS metric, m_fb_cnt AS value FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day, 'M' AS gender, 'fb' AS channel, 'qty' AS metric, m_fb_qty AS value FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day, 'F' AS gender, 'tw' AS channel, 'cnt' AS metric, f_tw_cnt AS value FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day, 'F' AS gender, 'tw' AS channel, 'qty' AS metric, f_tw_qty AS value FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day, 'F' AS gender, 'fb' AS channel, 'cnt' AS metric, f_fb_cnt AS value FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day, 'F' AS gender, 'fb' AS channel, 'qty' AS metric, f_fb_qty AS value FROM web_demographics
accepted.description: Unpivot daily demographic channel/gender counters and quantities into one row per day/gender/channel/metric. Useful for flexible filtering by gender or channel. | Use for: Filter demographic metrics by gender or channel; Compare counts vs quantities across channels; Join demographic slices to web device or counter data by day

accepted.name: latest_hire_period_per_emp
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT ehp.emp_id AS emp_id, ehp.start_ AS start_, ehp.end_ AS end_, ehp.title AS title
FROM emp_hire_periods ehp
INNER JOIN (
  SELECT emp_id, MAX(start_) AS max_start
  FROM emp_hire_periods
  GROUP BY emp_id
) m ON ehp.emp_id = m.emp_id AND ehp.start_ = m.max_start
accepted.description: Select the latest emp_hire_period row per emp_id by start_ (most recent start_). Useful for resolving current title when employees have multiple hire periods. | Use for: Report current employee title; Join employee current title to picking_list or picking activity; Build org charts or supervisor reports using latest title

accepted.name: picking_activity_with_employee
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  plog.picklist_id AS picklist_id,
  plog.log_time AS log_time,
  plog.activity AS activity,
  plog.location_id AS location_id,
  plog.pickline_no AS pickline_no,
  pl.created AS created,
  pl.picker_emp_id AS picker_emp_id,
  e.name AS name,
  e.title AS title
FROM picking_log plog
LEFT JOIN picking_list pl ON plog.picklist_id = pl.id
LEFT JOIN employees e ON pl.picker_emp_id = e.id
accepted.description: Picking log activity joined to picklists and employees (picker). Useful for operational audit, picker performance, and timeline analyses. | Use for: Analyze picker performance and activity timelines; Audit picking actions per picklist; Join picking events to locations and pick lines for reconciliation

accepted.name: purchases_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.id AS id,
  p.purchased AS purchased,
  p.brewery_id AS brewery_id,
  b.name AS name_brewery,
  p.product_id AS product_id,
  pr.name AS name_product,
  p.qty AS qty,
  p.cost AS cost
FROM purchases p
LEFT JOIN breweries b ON p.brewery_id = b.id
LEFT JOIN products pr ON p.product_id = pr.id
accepted.description: Purchases joined to products and breweries exposing product/brewery names with purchase measures. Useful for cost analysis and supplier reporting. | Use for: Analyze purchase costs by supplier or product; Reconcile purchases to inventory via purchase_id; Compute average cost per product over time

accepted.name: product_alcohol_with_product
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  pa.product_id AS product_id,
  pa.sales_volume AS sales_volume,
  pa.abv AS abv,
  p.name AS name
FROM product_alcohol pa
LEFT JOIN products p ON pa.product_id = p.id
accepted.description: Product alcohol and volume data joined to product metadata. Useful when computing alcohol-weighted sales or filtering by abv/sales_volume. | Use for: Compute alcohol-by-volume weighted metrics; Filter products by abv and join to sales/inventory
